observations_used: Round 3 discovered a new global area/WNS Pareto point: (10,4,2), area 327.18, WNS 7.52158.
(10,4,2) strictly dominates the previous minimum-area frontier point (12,4).
For first-block width 10, moving from (10,2,4) through (10,3,3) to (10,4,2) improved WNS and ultimately reduced area substantially.
(13,2,1) retained high timing at WNS 7.56610, suggesting that some one-bit tails can be useful.
Three-block architectures are therefore not generally inferior; their exact partition strongly affects physical QoR.
hypothesis: Continuing the shift toward a larger middle block and smaller final block may either extend the low-area frontier or recover enough timing to improve scalar reward.

proposals.rationale: Move one bit from the strong (10,4,2) first block into its middle block while retaining the 2-bit tail; probe for a further area reduction.
Direct continuation of the observed (10,2,4) -> (10,3,3) -> (10,4,2) progression.
Continue the high-timing diagonal toward a one-bit tail from the measured (11,3,2) structure.
